newsitem.title: USA: Chi says Chinese arms proliferation "exaggerated". [CORRECTED 15:55 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Chi says Chinese arms proliferation "exaggerated". [CORRECTED 15:55 GMT]

text.p: News reports have exaggerated the issues of nuclear and missile proliferation by China, and some of those problems "simply do not exist," Chinese Defence Minister Chi Haotian (corrects from Haotain) said at the Pentagon on Monday.

Chi told reporters as he was welcomed by Defence Secretary William Perry at the start of high-level talks with U.S. officials that Beijing had made clear it was anxious to refrain from doing anything to harm world peace and security.
The United States has protested to China in the past about alleged sales of missile and arms technology to Pakistan that might advance Pakistan's nuclear arms programme.
Recent published reports have also said Washington is worried about Chinese arms transfers to Iran.

"I think on some of such issues the media have blown the issue of proportion, have exaggerated the issue," Chi said in a question from reporters at a brief joint news conference outside U.S. Defence Department headquarters after a colourful welcoming ceremony.

"Some of the issues have been exaggerated and some of these issues simply do not exist," he said, adding that China had carefully guarded its technology exports under the so-called Missile Technology Control Regime.

But Perry said controversy over arms transfers would be a key subject of discussion on Monday. He also said China and the United States must cooperate "to prevent any weapons of mass destruction or the materials for those weapons from being proliferated to other countries."
